newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Treasury sets state notes coupons.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Treasury sets state notes coupons.

text.p: The Belgian Treasury said on Monday it would re-open two June state note issues for September issuance under its state notes programme.
As a result of what it called unchanged market conditions it was leaving coupons on the issues steady.
For five-year state notes, extendable to seven years, the coupon was kept at 4.70 percent.

The first coupon for the 3/5/7 note, which bears put options at three, five and seven years and a guaranteed minimum coupon, was 3.85 percent. The second and third coupons were 4.70 and 5.35 percent respectively.
Subscriptions open on August 26 and close on September 3. Payment is due on September 4.
The Treasury said in a statement BELJ that the new issues would have short first coupons of nine months and would be second tranches of the June 4, 1997 issues.
The June and September issues will have matching payment dates for coupon and final maturity and thus become fungible after the payment of the first coupon.

The June issues, which were sold at par, raised 8.175 billion francs. Belgium hopes to raise 54 billion francs from a total of four issues planned for 1997/1998. Last year it raised 53 billion francs when it had targeted 80 billion.
The notes are aimed at retail investors in direct competition with commercial banks' savings, or "cash", bonds, traditionally Belgium's most popular investment vehicle.
